title: James Talarico Wins Texas Senate Seat, a First for Democrats Since 1988
summary:
Democrat James Talarico has won a Senate race in Texas, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the state since 1988.

Talarico, a former schoolteacher and state legislator, defeated Republican Ken Paxton. His victory helped Democrats take full control of Congress in a night of wins across the country.

Talarico was little known nationally until last year. He made the rising cost of living a central theme of his campaign. Paxton, who campaigned alongside President Trump several times, argued that Talarico's views were too progressive for Texas.

Supporters at a watch party in Austin, the state capital, celebrated loudly when television projections called the race for Talarico. "We just proved that all the money in the world is no match for the people of Texas," he told them, referring to the huge spending in the race.

The contest became the most expensive U.S. Senate race in history, with more than half a billion dollars spent. Billionaire Elon Musk gave $158 million to a political group supporting Paxton, a point Talarico raised often in his attacks on Paxton's campaign.

In another surprise, two members of the Bush family, a Republican political dynasty with deep Texas roots, backed Talarico.

For decades, a Democrat winning statewide in Texas had seemed out of reach. Texas, the nation's second most populous state, has long been a stronghold of conservatism, and its Republican policies are often copied elsewhere.

Talarico compared his unlikely odds to the biblical story of David and Goliath. "This win is for every Texan who's ever wondered if anyone is listening," he said.

The same night, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott, the first Democrat to win the governor's race there since the 1990s.
why_it_matters: A single Senate seat can help decide control of Congress, and this result shows that even the most expensive campaign in history can be beaten by a little-known candidate.

background_read: The U.S. Senate is one of the two chambers of Congress, with two senators from every state, and each seat is filled by a statewide election.
Texas is the nation's second most populous state and has usually voted Republican in statewide races, which is why a Democratic win there is rare.
Big Senate races attract enormous spending because a single seat can help decide which party controls the whole Senate.
